# Reports

`hub report` and the MCP tool `hub_report` take lines. A prefix sends each line to the card section or the log it belongs to; nothing is guessed. One report is one call, however many lines it has.

## The template

`hub report --agent <you>` with no input prints it:

```text
# Session report — one item per line, then pipe back in (heredoc) or pass with -m.
# Each prefix routes into the project card; unprefixed lines become a NOTE.
# Do NOT list files/commits — "what changed" is read from git by `hub brief`.

DECIDE: <what> | <why>        # → ## Decisions  (repeat for each decision)
FACT:   <reusable fact learned>   # → ## Facts & hypotheses
HYPO:   <belief, not yet proven>  # → ## Facts & hypotheses
COMM:   <what went out / queued>  # → ## Communication
NEXT:   <the single next action>  # → ## Next step (set)
DONE:   <task-ids, comma-sep>     # closes tasks
TASK:   <new task text>           # opens a task
NOTE:   <one-line anything-else>
HANDOFF: <where your work stands, the next step>  # → ## Handoff <you> (set)

# Example:  hub report -p hubd <<EOF
#   DECIDE: ship docs in the release | npm README drifted
#   FACT: registry JWT expires in minutes
#   NEXT: redeploy vm1 under 0.1.8
#   DONE: 42, 43
#   EOF
```

## Prefixes

A prefix is a word and a colon at the start of a line, in any case: `fact:` is `FACT:`. A line without one is a note.

| Prefix | Also | Where the line goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DECIDE:` | `DECISION:` | appended to `## Decisions` as `- <time>: <what> — <why>`, split at the first `\|`; also journaled as a decision |
| `FACT:` | `GOTCHA:`, `LEARNED:`, `LEARN:`, `DISCOVERY:` | appended to `## Facts & hypotheses` as `- fact: <text>` |
| `HYPO:` | `HYPOTHESIS:` | appended to `## Facts & hypotheses` as `- hypothesis: <text>` |
| `COMM:` | `COMMS:`, `COMMUNICATION:`, `SHIPPED:` | appended to `## Communication`, dated |
| `NEXT:` |  | replaces `## Next step` with the step, its time and its author, and keeps the step before as one `prev` line. A step an owner role set is replaced by no one else without `force` (`--force`) |
| `DONE:` | `CLOSED:`, `CLOSE:` | closes the tasks it names, comma-separated: each id as `hub task list` shows it, `#` optional, or the bare number when one task ends in it. The reply says what closed, what was closed already, and what matched nothing |
| `TASK:` | `TODO:` | opens a task in the project |
| `NOTE:` |  | the journal: one entry, the report's note lines joined by ` · `. A line with no prefix is a note too |
| `HANDOFF:` |  | replaces the author's own `## Handoff <agent>` section with one dated entry, the lines after the first as its continuation, and journals them as one `handoff` entry. Refused whole when it would not fit the section cap. `hub_context` and `hub whereami` return it to the next session with its age |
| `TO:` |  | whom the journal entry is for: a role, or `fleet`. The entry stays public; readers filter on it |

## The rest of a report

- **Project**: `-p` (`project`) names the card; the default is `general`.
- **Kind** of the journal entry, `note` when none is given: over MCP one of `done`, `broken`, `blocked`, `note`; the CLI's `-k` takes any word (a mail relay files `delivery`).
- **Private**: `--private` (`private: true`) puts the note in `journal.life.jsonl`, on this node only. Prose only: a prefixed line would write a card, and cards sync, so the two together are refused.
- **The reply** says how old the card's digest is (`digestAgeDays`) and, once it trails the project's journal by `staleDays` (7 by default), says so (`digestStale`) with the command that fixes it.
- **A section over its size limit** (`limits.json`, `card.sectionBytes`) moves its oldest entries to `projects/history/<slug>.md` on the write that grew it.
- **The card write** is recorded on a journal entry the report files anyway: its last decision, else its note. A report with neither files an entry of kind `card` for it (`card reported: FACT ×2 · NEXT — <the first line>`). The entry's `card` field names the sections written, the size of the card file after the write in bytes, and the change. Every other card write records itself the same way: `hub card`, `hub section add`, `hub sync`, an accepted law, `hub cards merge`, `compact` and `merge-sections`. A card that reads older than a write is checked with `hub_whatsnew` or `hub log`, not with git. A `card` entry is bookkeeping and does not move the project's journal on for the digest's age.

## Refused

- A line that reads as closing a task but is not the `DONE:` form (`#471 DONE`, `DONE #471`): it would close nothing, so the report is refused and the reply gives the form.
- A report of prose only, when `rules.json` turns on `strict.rejectNoteOnlyReport`. Off by default.
- A private report with a prefixed line (above).
- Cargo instead of prose, and a report over `HUBD_MSG_MAX` ([Environment](env.md)).

## Reflections

A turn ends with a reflection on its one report: a block at the end of the text, or the same fields as `reflect` (MCP) or `--reflect <json|file>` (CLI). The field is checked and the whole report refused on a value off its list; a block in the text is read, never refused, and the reply lists what a digest could not use. A turn that only waits for a dispatch takes no reflection. The block opens with `REFLECT`, `HEAD-REFLECT`, `FLEET-REFLECT`, by level:

```text
REFLECT
goal: wire the hosted payment page into checkout
result: partial
obstacle: environment — staging answered 502 to 3 of 10 calls
instead: check the staging health page before a payment test
rule: check staging health before a payment test
```

```text
HEAD-REFLECT
goal: checkout live on staging
result: done
obstacle: none
instead: nothing
rule: none
decision: accepted — check staging health before a payment test
```

| Field | Required | Values | What |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` |  | `turn`, `head`, `fleet` | turn (default): this turn, any role; head: a head's over its workers; fleet: the orchestrator's over the heads |
| `goal` | yes | text | what the turn was meant to deliver |
| `result` | yes | `done`, `partial`, `no` | done only if this report names an artifact |
| `obstacle` | yes | `permissions`, `path`, `unclear-dispatch`, `environment`, `model`, `none` |  |
| `obstacle_fact` |  | text | the fact with a number or a quote (exit code, seconds, refusal text), or "not measured"; required unless obstacle is none, refused with none |
| `instead` | yes | text | what you would do differently |
| `rule` | yes | text | one rule for the prompt, or "none" |
| `decisions` |  | a list of `{rule, verdict, reason}`, the verdict one of `accepted`, `rejected`, `needs-owner` | head and fleet only: the verdict on each proposal from below |

- `obstacle` `none` takes no `obstacle_fact`; any other obstacle needs one, or `not measured`.
- `result` `no` with `obstacle` `none` is refused: a turn that delivered nothing names what held it up.
- `instead` `nothing` only with `result` `done` and `obstacle` `none`.
- `rule` is one rule: a `;` outside backticks makes it several, refused. `none` when the turn taught none. The example's rule ("keep build recipes only inside the role's allowed paths") is refused: it is not this turn's.
- `decisions` only at level `head` or `fleet`.

## From rules to laws

`hub reflect --promote` (`hub_reflect` with `promote`) lists a rule as a candidate for the project's laws once one role said it 3 times, or 2 roles said it, in the window (7 days by default). Two wordings count as one rule when 40% of their words are shared, a word compared by its first five letters. The head accepts a candidate by its id (`hub reflect --accept`, `hub_law`) into the card's `## Laws`, which `hub_context` returns to every role, or rejects it; a rejected rule comes back only if it keeps being said after the rejection. Walk-through: [6. Laws](../start/6-laws.md).
